programs.notes: EPOCH in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer disease and APECS in prodromal Alzheimer disease were separate terminated phase 3 trials of the BACE1 inhibitor verubecestat. EPOCH was stopped for futility without slowing cognitive or functional decline; APECS was stopped for futility without benefit on its CDR-SB primary clinical outcome. Neither registry termination status alone establishes the reason.

Gamma-secretase-directed development; primary protein assignment unresolved. Experimental work found pseudo-inhibition distinct from presenilin loss of function; do not interpret the trial outcome as a PSEN1-specific target failure. One representative trial linked.

The initial NCT04032171 protocol ended in 2020 to change the active comparator; it was not an efficacy failure. The subsequent evolutionRMS 1 and 2 phase 3 trials failed to show superiority to teriflunomide on annualized relapse rate and were terminated after primary analysis.

Primary protein target is unclear. Iniparib was historically described as a PARP inhibitor but experimental studies found no bona fide PARP inhibition and nonspecific modification of many cysteine-containing proteins. The negative trial outcome must not be interpreted as failure of PARP1 inhibition.

HSP90 inhibitor with alpha and beta isoform engagement; no unique primary isoform assigned. NCT00773344 studied tanespimycin with trastuzumab; the formerly linked NCT00627627 studied retaspimycin and was removed. No tanespimycin failure conclusion is supported by this registry record.

The JAMA report of STARSHINE STARBEAM and STARBRIGHT found no significant cognitive benefit on the prespecified ADAS-Cog primary endpoint in any of the three completed phase 3 trials. Target identity was corrected to the reviewed human HTR6 UniProt accession P50406; Q9Y5N1 belongs to HRH3 and must not be used for this drug.

TRINOVA-1 met its primary PFS endpoint; TRINOVA-2 and TRINOVA-3 did not improve their primary PFS endpoints. Later registry termination of long-term follow-up in TRINOVA-2/3 is separate from those efficacy findings. NCT00467025 was removed from this ovarian program because it is a phase 2 renal-cell-carcinoma study. Trebananib directly engages both ANGPT1 and ANGPT2; neither is designated the unique primary protein target. Broader program disposition remains under review.

The adenosine A1 receptor antagonist was evaluated in the paired PROTECT-1 and PROTECT-2 phase 3 protocols. The combined primary publication found no significant benefit on the prespecified three-category clinical outcome versus placebo. Both registry protocols completed; safety findings are not substituted for the primary efficacy result.

The monovalent anti-MET antibody was combined with erlotinib in the completed METLung phase 3 trial after prior platinum chemotherapy. The primary overall-survival endpoint was not improved versus placebo plus erlotinib; median OS was numerically shorter in the onartuzumab arm. The row previously misclassified this antibody as a small molecule.

DLL3-directed antibody-drug conjugate. MERU maintenance therapy was terminated after overall-survival futility in DLL3-high disease; TAHOE second-line therapy completed with inferior overall survival versus topotecan. Trial outcomes are distinct and should not be collapsed into a generic stop reason.
Promoted pilot batch; verify all program-level evidence before publication.

The published BRISK-PS negative overall-survival result belongs to completed NCT00825955. NCT01108705 was a distinct Asia-Pacific phase 3 study marked terminated in the registry without a stated why-stopped reason; it must not inherit the BRISK-PS endpoint result. Bristol Myers Squibb reported termination of the broader brivanib program during 2012 but did not attribute this protocol's stop to a specific endpoint or decision. Brivanib inhibits VEGFR and FGFR proteins without a unique primary protein assignment. The separate renal-cell-carcinoma NCT01253668 protocol is not part of this indication-level program.

NCT01253668 enrolled 10 participants and was terminated after the manufacturer decided not to pursue additional research in this patient population. Its posted outcome data were unavailable after the principal investigator left the institution; no failed efficacy endpoint is established. This is distinct from brivanib's HCC trials.

The randomized phase 3 NCT01009593 trial failed its prespecified overall-survival superiority and noninferiority criteria versus sorafenib. Time to progression and response rate favored linifanib while adverse events were more frequent. The registry says an independent monitoring committee recommended stopping but does not state a more specific stopping rationale. Linifanib inhibits VEGF and PDGF receptor families; no single primary receptor is assigned and the clinical result is not a single-protein target failure.

NCT00360867 was a safety-focused extension for patients coming from other motesanib protocols; it was not a randomized efficacy trial. The registry reports termination by Amgen decision without a specific efficacy or safety cause for this extension. This record must not inherit MONET1's NSCLC outcome. Motesanib inhibits several receptor kinases without one clinically established primary protein.

MONET1/NCT00460317 first enrolled squamous and nonsquamous NSCLC. Treatment and enrollment in the squamous cohort stopped after excess early deaths and fatal bleeding with motesanib. The amended nonsquamous comparison did not significantly improve overall survival versus chemotherapy alone despite favorable PFS and response-rate signals. The registry says Amgen discontinued development because MONET1 missed its primary objective. These regimen- and histology-specific findings are not failures attributable to one VEGFR or other protein.

NCT01799889 included several lymphoma and CLL cohorts. Gilead's registry states the trial ended after its decision to discontinue entospletinib development; this is not a demonstrated efficacy-endpoint failure. Published CLL subcohorts reported responses. Cohort-specific outcomes and later development under other sponsors require separate review.

programs.indication_name: newly diagnosed NPM1-mutated acute myeloid leukemia
programs.notes: AGILITY/NCT05020665 tested entospletinib plus intensive chemotherapy. Kronos Bio stopped enrollment before the planned sample was reached because recruiting fit patients with NPM1-mutated AML was difficult and post-COVID constraints persisted. The registry and sponsor do not attribute the stop to a failed efficacy endpoint; this is separate from Gilead's earlier relapsed-hematology phase 2 program.

EGFR-directed antibody-drug conjugate. INTELLANCE-1/NCT02573324 was a completed phase 3 survival trial that stopped treatment early after an interim overall-survival futility finding. UNITE/NCT03419403 was a separate phase 3b ocular-prophylaxis study terminated after that cross-study decision; it did not fail a survival primary endpoint. These are distinct trial outcomes within one indication-level program.

GPNMB-directed antibody-drug conjugate. PrECOG 0504 was registered as phase 1/2 but only the phase 1 dose-finding portion enrolled; the planned phase 2 portion was not undertaken after the company discontinued development for this indication. This is not classified as an efficacy endpoint failure.

Single primary protein target remains unresolved. NCT02730884 terminated at investigator request due to low accrual with three enrolled; this is a recruitment event and not evidence of lack of efficacy.

programs.indication_name: relapsed or refractory germ cell tumors
programs.notes: Single primary clinical mechanism is unresolved. NCT01055067 stopped for futility under its prespecified Simon two-stage rule; this is an indication-specific event and does not establish MET target failure.

IL-6 binding mechanism confirmed by approved product information SRC-FDA-siltuximab-label. NCT01266811 was a planned phase 3 study withdrawn before enrollment based on another study; it is not evidence of endpoint failure in this trial. Program remains under review for broader myeloma development.

Two separate phase 2 protocols are distinguished. Completed NCT00513071 found zero qualifying PSA responses among 28 patients. Later NCT01267266 stopped after only eight of 31 treated patients reached randomization following a saracatinib lead-in; its planned randomized efficacy comparison was not adequately tested. Saracatinib inhibits Fyn and other Src-family kinases without one established primary protein assignment; neither trial is a single-protein target-failure demonstration.

Balovaptan selectively antagonizes the V1a receptor (AVPR1A). VANILLA phase 2 in adult men missed its SRS-2 primary endpoint despite a favorable Vineland-II secondary signal. Pediatric aV1ation phase 2 and adult V1aduct phase 3 did not improve their Vineland-II two-domain primary endpoints versus placebo; V1aduct stopped after interim futility. The linked phase 3 record includes an open-label extension but is not an extension-only trial. These are indication- and population-specific outcomes, not proof that AVPR1A is biologically invalid.

programs.indication_name: coronary heart disease and acute coronary syndrome
programs.notes: Darapladib selectively inhibits lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 encoded by PLA2G7. Completed STABILITY and SOLID-TIMI 52 phase 3 trials did not improve their respective primary cardiovascular outcomes; the separate Mayo endothelial-function trial was also negative. The target is not the secretory PLA2 family inhibited by varespladib.

programs.indication_name: previously treated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer
programs.notes: NCT03228186 reported objective responses in a single-arm phase 2 study; its registry says the trial stopped because the pharmaceutical company discontinued the study drug. The observed response rate is not an efficacy-endpoint failure and the registry does not establish why the company made its broader drug decision. Pevonedistat inhibits the NEDD8-activating enzyme complex; no unique primary protein is assigned here.

NCT03319537 is a separate phase 1/2 mesothelioma study with efficacy and dose-finding cohorts; it must not be attributed to the lung-cancer program. Registry termination reason is sponsor termination of the study agreement; an efficacy-endpoint failure is not established.

The completed U.S. Act-Earli-AD phase 3 trial NCT00105547 found no benefit on either co-primary cognition or activities-of-daily-living outcome. Myriad then discontinued Flurizan development; the separate global phase 3 NCT00322036 and open-label safety extension NCT00380276 were terminated after that portfolio decision and must not be counted as independent failed efficacy trials. Tarenflurbil was developed as an amyloid-beta-42-lowering gamma-secretase modulator but a unique directly engaged primary protein remains unresolved; this is not a PSEN1-specific target failure.

The early NCT00948259 trial primarily evaluated safety and tolerability. The separate ARGO phase 2 NCT01350362 study did not show significant clinical efficacy. Biochemical studies document GSK3B and GSK3A inhibition but do not establish a unique primary protein mediating the clinical effect.

The phase 2/3 REACH CDM trial NCT03692312 completed. Its registered primary CDM1-RS comparison did not reach conventional statistical significance (p=0.0514) while some secondary outcomes favored tideglusib. Biochemical studies document GSK3B and GSK3A inhibition but do not establish a unique clinical primary protein. Do not infer that the entire development program was discontinued from this result alone.

programs.indication_name: coronary artery disease and acute coronary syndrome
programs.notes: PLASMA and FRANCIS-ACS reported favorable prespecified biomarker outcomes but did not establish fewer clinical cardiovascular events. Later VISTA-16 stopped for futility and possible harm with higher myocardial infarction risk. Varespladib inhibits several secretory phospholipase A2 isoforms; no unique primary protein is assigned and this is not a PLA2G7 failure. The separate intravenous sickle-cell NCT01522196 protocol is recorded under its own indication-level program.

programs.indication_name: sickle cell disease with vaso-occlusive crisis
programs.notes: IMPACTS-2/NCT01522196 studied prevention of acute chest syndrome with intravenous varespladib and enrolled two participants. The registry says the study terminated because of a change in company plans; it does not establish an efficacy-endpoint failure or explicitly attribute this decision to VISTA-16.
GRADUATE I and II; antibody binds aggregated amyloid beta represented by the APP target row; trial status and endpoint result are separate fields.
MISSION AD1 and AD2; Eisai and Biogen discontinued development after an unfavorable benefit-risk review.

programs.indication_name: asymptomatic amyloid-positive and early Alzheimer disease
programs.notes: EARLY phase 2b/3 and its phase 2 long-term extension; dosing stopped in May 2018 after liver-enzyme elevations changed the sponsor's benefit-risk assessment. Do not interpret post-termination efficacy analyses as the original stopping rationale.

LUSTER-1 and LUSTER-2 tested exacerbations in severe asthma; ZEAL-1 and ZEAL-2 tested lung function in less severe uncontrolled asthma. All four phase 3 trials completed without meeting their respective efficacy endpoints; Novartis stopped further asthma development.

programs.indication_name: geographic atrophy due to age-related macular degeneration
programs.notes: CHROMA and SPECTRI phase 3 trials; intravitreal anti-complement factor D Fab did not reduce geographic atrophy enlargement versus sham in the week-48 primary analysis.

Completed phase 3 osteoarthritis studies included efficacy signals and joint safety concerns. Pfizer and Lilly discontinued global development in October 2021 after an FDA Complete Response Letter and negative EMA CHMP opinion; do not label the representative trials as endpoint failures.

programs.indication_name: moderately to severely active systemic lupus erythematosus
programs.notes: EMBODY 1 and EMBODY 2 completed phase 3 trials; neither achieved a statistically significant week-48 BICLA primary endpoint versus placebo. Earlier ALLEVIATE supply interruption is not conflated with these efficacy results.

programs.indication_name: moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis
programs.notes: SIRROUND-D and SIRROUND-T completed phase 3 trials with positive efficacy results. A subsequent FDA Complete Response Letter sought additional safety data; Janssen then did not pursue global RA approvals and withdrew its EMA application. This is not an efficacy-endpoint failure.

SYNERGY completed phase 2 with a negative primary endpoint; development continued into AFFINITY. AFFINITY Part 1 then missed its primary and key secondary endpoints; the registry marks the combined Part 1/2 protocol terminated because Part 2 was discontinued. Biogen discontinued opicinumab development in October 2020; registry states the Part 2 stop was not based on safety concerns.

The phase 2 SPARK trial tested anti-alpha-synuclein antibody cinpanemab. Registry status is terminated following negative year-1 primary and secondary outcomes; the primary publication reports no clinical or DaT-SPECT benefit and a lack-of-efficacy stop after interim review. Biogen separately reported program discontinuation in February 2021.

PASSPORT tested anti-N-terminal-tau antibody gosuranemab and did not meet its week-52 PSP Rating Scale primary endpoint. The registry labels the study terminated after that result and states there were no safety concerns. Biogen stopped development for PSP and other primary tauopathies but continued the separate TANGO Alzheimer disease study at that time; do not present this as an all-indication stop.

programs.indication_name: advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma
programs.notes: GAMMA-1 evaluated anti-MMP9 andecaliximab added to mFOLFOX6 as first-line therapy. The phase 3 protocol completed; the primary overall-survival endpoint was not improved versus placebo plus mFOLFOX6. A response-rate signal did not translate into an overall-survival benefit.

TANGO is a separate indication-specific program from PASSPORT. Its protocol lists safety as the primary objective; the prespecified week-78 CDR-SB efficacy endpoint was not met and the registry says the study was terminated after lack of efficacy following the placebo-controlled readout. Do not imply the primary safety endpoint failed.

The anti-tau phase 2 PSP study was terminated after prespecified interim futility criteria were met. The primary publication found no week-52 PSP Rating Scale benefit versus placebo. The clinical trial stop is attributed to lack of efficacy rather than a safety finding.

The RAINIER phase 2 trial tested an anti-LOXL2 antibody and was terminated when the second interim analysis met prespecified futility criteria. The primary publication found no improvement in progression-free survival

MINDSET was a completed phase 3 trial of the HTR6 antagonist intepirdine added to donepezil. The primary publication found no benefit on either co-primary ADAS-Cog or ADCS-ADL endpoint over 24 weeks. Registry completion is not itself the endpoint outcome.

LIGHT phase 3 trial; the IDMC recommended discontinuation and treatment ended. Publication reports that prespecified overall-survival superiority and noninferiority criteria versus sorafenib were not met.
Safety-focused open-label treatment extension (n=94) terminated by Amgen decision; the registry gives no further reason and does not establish an efficacy failure in this protocol.

MONET1 phase 3 (n=1450 total): squamous enrollment/treatment stopped after early mortality and bleeding; later nonsquamous primary overall-survival comparison missed its objective. Registry attributes development discontinuation to the missed primary objective.
The sponsor discontinued development under this protocol; published CLL cohorts showed responses but heterogeneous cohort-level outcomes should not be condensed into an efficacy-failure label.

AGILITY enrollment ended early because the sponsor reported recruitment difficulties in a genetically selected fit AML population and post-COVID constraints; no primary efficacy-endpoint failure is established.
UNITE phase 3b studied ocular-side-effect prophylaxis; enrollment stopped after the separate INTELLANCE-1 survival-futility result. This was not a UNITE survival endpoint failure.
Registered phase 1/2 protocol; only phase 1 dose-finding enrolled. Planned phase 2 did not proceed after company discontinued development for the indication.
Terminated at investigator request due to low accrual; three enrolled.
Stopped early for futility under Simon two-stage rule; no complete or partial responses among 21 stage-one participants.
The single-arm study recorded zero qualifying PSA responses among 28 patients; the published report found little clinical efficacy as monotherapy.

Only eight of 31 treated patients reached randomization after the lead-in; a prespecified low-randomization futility rule ended the study before the planned randomized metastasis comparison was adequately tested.
aV1ation pediatric phase 2; registry says the 24-week primary endpoint showed no clinical or statistical benefit and no new safety concerns.
Mayo endothelial-function study completed without improvement in prespecified coronary endothelial-function outcomes; it is distinct from STABILITY and SOLID-TIMI 52.
The published single-arm trial reported a 22% objective response rate (1 complete and 5 partial responses); the registry says termination followed company discontinuation of the study drug.
Global phase 3 efficacy study terminated after Myriad discontinued Flurizan development following the separate negative U.S. trial; no independent global primary-endpoint failure is established.
The U.S. Act-Earli-AD trial found no benefit on either co-primary cognition or activities-of-daily-living outcome at 18 months.
Open-label safety extension terminated after Myriad discontinued Flurizan development; this protocol did not test an efficacy primary endpoint.
V1aduct adult randomized phase 3 efficacy trial with a planned open-label extension; registry says interim futility made the predefined primary objective highly unlikely, with no new safety concerns.
VANILLA adult-male phase 2; primary SRS-2 outcome not improved versus placebo at week 12, despite a favorable secondary Vineland-II adaptive-behavior signal.
Registered phase 1/2 mesothelioma protocol ended after sponsor termination of the study agreement; registry result posting does not establish an efficacy-driven stop.

TRINOVA-3: primary PFS was not improved; registry termination refers to later administrative long-term follow-up closure.
TRINOVA-1 met its primary PFS endpoint: median 7.2 versus 5.4 months with trebananib versus placebo plus paclitaxel.

SPARK did not meet its year-1 MDS-UPDRS primary endpoint or secondary outcomes; the trial was stopped for lack of efficacy.
PASSPORT did not meet its week-52 PSP Rating Scale primary endpoint; registry reports early closure without a safety concern.

Published BRISK-PS phase 3 trial NCT00825955 found no statistically significant overall-survival improvement with brivanib versus placebo plus best supportive care after sorafenib failure or intolerance.
The separate Asia-Pacific BRISK-APS study is marked terminated but its registry does not state a reason; the BRISK-PS endpoint result must not be copied to this protocol.

Bristol Myers Squibb disclosed that it terminated the broader brivanib development program during 2012. The filing does not identify a protocol-specific stopping cause for BRISK-APS or establish an independent BRISK-APS endpoint failure.

LIGHT phase 3 (n=1035) did not meet its prespecified overall-survival superiority or noninferiority criteria versus sorafenib (median 9.1 vs 9.8 months; HR 1.046, 95% CI 0.896-1.221). Time to progression and response rate favored linifanib, but serious and grade 3/4 adverse events were more frequent. The registry records IDMC-recommended discontinuation without a more specific stated stopping rationale; this event describes the published endpoint result, not an inferred stopping cause.

The safety-focused extension enrolled patients continuing motesanib from other trials and was terminated by Amgen decision. The registry gives no protocol-specific efficacy or safety cause; MONET1's outcome is not assigned to this extension.

MONET1's amended nonsquamous NSCLC population (n=1090) did not have significantly improved overall survival with motesanib plus carboplatin/paclitaxel versus chemotherapy alone (median 13.0 vs 11.0 months; HR 0.90; p=0.14). PFS and response rate favored motesanib, while severe adverse events were more frequent. The registry states that Amgen discontinued development because the study missed its primary objective.

Within the same MONET1 protocol, squamous-histology enrollment and treatment stopped after higher early mortality and gross hemoptysis with motesanib. The squamous-cohort publication reports 23/182 versus 10/178 fatal adverse events within 60 days and six versus zero fatal bleeding events. This is a cohort-specific safety event, not a separate trial or the nonsquamous efficacy endpoint.

Gilead states it terminated the multi-cohort phase 2 study after deciding to discontinue its entospletinib development; the registry does not state that a prespecified efficacy endpoint failed. Published CLL cohorts reported clinical activity.

Kronos Bio terminated AGILITY enrollment before its planned sample because recruiting fit participants with NPM1-mutated AML was difficult and post-COVID constraints persisted; this is not a reported primary efficacy-endpoint failure.
UNITE ocular-side-effect prophylaxis enrollment stopped after the separate INTELLANCE-1 survival analysis showed no benefit; UNITE did not itself test or fail a survival primary endpoint.

The phase 1 dose-finding portion reported modest activity and a recommended phase 2 dose; the planned phase 2 portion was not undertaken because the company discontinued development for this indication. The registry labels the protocol terminated for that company decision.
NCT02730884 terminated at investigator request due to low accrual; three participants enrolled. This does not imply efficacy failure.
NCT01055067 stopped for futility under its Simon two-stage rule after no complete or partial responses in stage one.

The planned phase 3 study was withdrawn before enrollment (0 participants). The sponsor attributed cancellation to results of a different study with a similar hypothesis and agent; no efficacy endpoint was tested in NCT01266811.
Completed phase 2 saracatinib monotherapy study reported no qualifying PSA responses among 28 patients; its prespecified PSA response signal was not observed.

The later randomized-discontinuation study ended under its lead-in futility rule because only eight of 31 treated patients remained stable enough for randomization. The planned randomized comparison was therefore not adequately tested; this is not an observed failure of that primary comparison.

aV1ation pediatric phase 2 did not improve the prespecified Vineland-II two-domain composite at week 24 versus placebo (primary-analysis treatment difference -0.16; p=0.91). Registry stopping text reports no clinical or statistical primary-endpoint benefit and no new safety concern.
STABILITY and SOLID-TIMI 52 completed without meeting their respective primary cardiovascular outcomes; the separate Mayo endothelial-function trial was also negative.

The NSCLC trial registry states that the pharmaceutical company discontinued the study drug; the published trial reported a 22% objective response rate and does not support labeling the protocol an efficacy-endpoint failure.
The global phase 3 study stopped after Myriad discontinued Flurizan development following the separate U.S. phase 3 failure; its own co-primary endpoints are not reported as failed.
The completed U.S. Act-Earli-AD phase 3 trial found no statistically significant benefit on either co-primary outcome: ADAS-Cog cognition or ADCS-ADL function.
The open-label safety extension stopped after Flurizan development was discontinued following the separate U.S. efficacy trial; it did not fail an efficacy primary endpoint.

V1aduct adult phase 3 stopped after an interim futility analysis found the predefined primary Vineland-II two-domain objective highly unlikely to be met. The interim treatment difference was -1.84 (95% CI -5.15 to 1.48); no new safety concern was identified. This is the randomized efficacy trial, not an independent extension failure.

VANILLA phase 2 in adult men did not improve its prespecified Social Responsiveness Scale-2 primary endpoint at week 12 versus placebo. The same publication reported a favorable dose-dependent secondary Vineland-II adaptive-behavior signal; that secondary finding does not turn the primary endpoint into a success.
Registry states the mesothelioma study ended when the sponsor terminated its study agreement; the underlying agreement rationale and whether an efficacy endpoint failed are not established.
Extension publication reports that parent Phase 3 protocols were stopped early for lack of efficacy.
CREAD 2 was discontinued after an interim analysis in the separate CREAD study indicated crenezumab was unlikely to meet its primary endpoint; CREAD 2 did not reach its own week 105 primary endpoint.

The manufacturer decided not to pursue additional brivanib research in metastatic renal cell carcinoma and requested closure to accrual. The registry reports unavailable outcome data after the investigator left; no primary efficacy-endpoint failure was established.
INTELLANCE-1 found no overall-survival benefit at its prespecified interim analysis and stopped early for futility; the reported PFS difference did not establish an OS benefit.

TRINOVA-2 did not improve its primary PFS endpoint (median 7.6 versus 7.2 months); ORR and duration of response improved. Enrollment was truncated after a PLD shortage; later registry termination described long-term follow-up closure, not the cause of the PFS result.

TRINOVA-3 did not improve primary PFS in first-line advanced ovarian cancer (15.9 versus 15.0 months; HR 0.93; p=0.36). Later administrative long-term follow-up closure should not be described as efficacy-driven trial termination.

No failure event is assigned to TRINOVA-1: its primary PFS endpoint was met (7.2 versus 5.4 months; HR 0.66; p<0.0001). This positive trial must not be collapsed into the negative TRINOVA-2/3 results.

Published phase I/IIa pilot (n=30) reported generally tolerable treatment; six active-treatment patients had moderate asymptomatic reversible transaminase elevations. Secondary cognitive trends were not statistically significant in this small trial. No stopping or efficacy-failure reason is assigned to this safety-focused study; the later ARGO efficacy result is a separate event.
The ARGO phase 2 publication reported no statistically significant clinical efficacy benefit in Alzheimer disease.

The IMPACTS-2 sickle-cell study terminated after enrolling two participants because of a registry-stated change in company plans; neither efficacy failure nor a specific connection to VISTA-16 is established.

The completed PLASMA study found a significant dose-dependent reduction in week-8 secretory phospholipase A2 group IIA concentration versus placebo. This surrogate biomarker response did not establish prevention of cardiovascular events.

The completed FRANCIS-ACS study met its week-8 LDL-cholesterol biomarker endpoint with varespladib plus atorvastatin versus placebo plus atorvastatin; secretory phospholipase A2 group IIA also fell. This phase 2 biomarker signal did not establish fewer major cardiovascular events.
Primary publication reported no improvement in coronary endothelial function in the registered trial.
The completed REACH CDM trial did not reach conventional significance on its registered primary CDM1-RS endpoint (p=0.0514); this does not establish discontinuation of the development program.
GRADUATE I did not meet its primary CDR-SB clinical endpoint; the registry lists the trial as terminated.
GRADUATE II did not meet its primary CDR-SB clinical endpoint; the registry lists the trial as terminated.
DSMB recommended discontinuation for an unfavorable benefit-risk balance; registry cites no evidence of potential efficacy and an adverse-event profile worse than placebo.
DSMB recommended discontinuation for an unfavorable benefit-risk balance; registry cites no evidence of potential efficacy and an adverse-event profile worse than placebo.

EARLY phase 2b/3 dosing and enrollment stopped after dose-related liver-enzyme elevations in atabecestat recipients changed the sponsor's benefit-risk assessment; subsequent cognitive analyses were not the original stopping trigger.
The phase 2 long-term extension was terminated as part of the atabecestat program stop after liver-enzyme elevations; this is not a separate failed efficacy endpoint.

LUSTER-1 completed but did not show a statistically significant reduction in moderate-to-severe asthma exacerbations after multiplicity adjustment; program development in asthma was then stopped after pooled LUSTER review.
LUSTER-2 completed but did not show a statistically significant reduction in moderate-to-severe asthma exacerbations after multiplicity adjustment; a numerical reduction does not establish success.
ZEAL-1 completed but did not meet the primary pre-dose FEV1 improvement endpoint at week 12; adjusted p=0.088 in the primary publication.
ZEAL-2 completed but did not meet the primary pre-dose FEV1 improvement endpoint at week 12; adjusted p=0.214 in the primary publication.
CHROMA phase 3 primary week-48 analysis found no reduction in geographic atrophy lesion enlargement with lampalizumab versus sham.
SPECTRI phase 3 primary week-48 analysis found no reduction in geographic atrophy lesion enlargement with lampalizumab versus sham; one regimen had a numerically worse lesion-area change.

Pfizer and Lilly discontinued global tanezumab development after an FDA Complete Response Letter for osteoarthritis and a negative EMA CHMP opinion. Joint safety concerns featured in regulatory review; representative phase 3 trials had efficacy signals and are not classified as endpoint failures.
EMBODY 1 completed but epratuzumab plus standard therapy did not significantly improve week-48 BICLA response versus placebo plus standard therapy.
EMBODY 2 completed but epratuzumab plus standard therapy did not significantly improve week-48 BICLA response versus placebo plus standard therapy.

Janssen reported an FDA Complete Response Letter for the RA BLA requesting additional clinical data to evaluate safety. The completed SIRROUND trials had efficacy signals and are not classified as endpoint failures.
Janssen withdrew the EMA marketing authorization application for RA; EMA reported outstanding concerns and the company cited the need for additional clinical data and portfolio prioritization.
SYNERGY missed its primary multicomponent endpoint for confirmed disability improvement; this event did not end development because AFFINITY followed.
AFFINITY Part 1 missed its primary and key secondary endpoints; the subsequent Part 2 termination was explicitly not attributed to safety concerns.
Biogen discontinued opicinumab development after the negative AFFINITY phase 2 results; this program decision is distinct from the SYNERGY and AFFINITY trial endpoint events.
SPARK showed no meaningful difference in MDS-UPDRS progression or DaT-SPECT imaging versus placebo; the trial stopped for lack of efficacy after interim analysis.
Biogen discontinued cinpanemab development after SPARK missed its primary and secondary endpoints; this is a separate program decision from the trial outcome.
PASSPORT showed no statistically significant improvement in week-52 PSP Rating Scale score versus placebo; key clinical secondary endpoints also lacked efficacy.
Biogen discontinued gosuranemab development for PSP and other primary tauopathies after PASSPORT while explicitly continuing the separate Alzheimer disease TANGO study.
GAMMA-1 completed without an overall-survival benefit from adding andecaliximab to mFOLFOX6 versus placebo plus mFOLFOX6; a higher response rate did not establish primary-endpoint success.

TANGO did not meet the prespecified week-78 CDR-SB efficacy endpoint and its extension was stopped for lack of efficacy; the protocol-listed primary outcomes were safety and tolerability and are not described as failed.
The PSP study met prespecified interim futility criteria and showed no significant week-52 PSP Rating Scale benefit with tilavonemab versus placebo.
RAINIER was terminated after its second interim analysis met prespecified futility criteria; simtuzumab did not improve progression-free survival in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
MINDSET completed but intepirdine plus donepezil did not significantly improve either co-primary week-24 ADAS-Cog cognition or ADCS-ADL function versus placebo plus donepezil.
APECS was terminated on a prespecified futility recommendation; verubecestat showed no benefit versus placebo on its CDR-SB primary clinical outcome in prodromal Alzheimer disease.
STABILITY completed but darapladib did not significantly reduce its primary cardiovascular death myocardial infarction or stroke composite versus placebo.
SOLID-TIMI 52 completed but darapladib did not significantly reduce its primary major coronary events composite after acute coronary syndrome.

VISTA-16 was stopped after prespecified interim review for futility and possible harm. The primary composite was not significantly improved and myocardial infarction risk was higher with varespladib than placebo; this is not a failure of the unrelated PLA2G7 target.

clinical_programs.notes: EPOCH in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer disease and APECS in prodromal Alzheimer disease were separate terminated phase 3 trials of the BACE1 inhibitor verubecestat. EPOCH was stopped for futility without slowing cognitive or functional decline; APECS was stopped for futility without benefit on its CDR-SB primary clinical outcome. Neither registry termination status alone establishes the reason.

Gamma-secretase-directed development; primary protein assignment unresolved. Experimental work found pseudo-inhibition distinct from presenilin loss of function; do not interpret the trial outcome as a PSEN1-specific target failure. One representative trial linked.
Pilot seed; one representative trial linked
Pilot seed; one representative trial linked

The initial NCT04032171 protocol ended in 2020 to change the active comparator; it was not an efficacy failure. The subsequent evolutionRMS 1 and 2 phase 3 trials failed to show superiority to teriflunomide on annualized relapse rate and were terminated after primary analysis.
Pilot seed; one representative trial linked

Primary protein target is unclear. Iniparib was historically described as a PARP inhibitor but experimental studies found no bona fide PARP inhibition and nonspecific modification of many cysteine-containing proteins. The negative trial outcome must not be interpreted as failure of PARP1 inhibition.
Pilot seed; one representative trial linked
Pilot seed; one representative trial linked

HSP90 inhibitor with alpha and beta isoform engagement; no unique primary isoform assigned. NCT00773344 studied tanespimycin with trastuzumab; the formerly linked NCT00627627 studied retaspimycin and was removed. No tanespimycin failure conclusion is supported by this registry record.
Promoted pilot batch; verify all program-level evidence before publication.
Promoted pilot batch; verify all program-level evidence before publication.

The JAMA report of STARSHINE STARBEAM and STARBRIGHT found no significant cognitive benefit on the prespecified ADAS-Cog primary endpoint in any of the three completed phase 3 trials. Target identity was corrected to the reviewed human HTR6 UniProt accession P50406; Q9Y5N1 belongs to HRH3 and must not be used for this drug.

TRINOVA-1 met its primary PFS endpoint; TRINOVA-2 and TRINOVA-3 did not improve their primary PFS endpoints. Later registry termination of long-term follow-up in TRINOVA-2/3 is separate from those efficacy findings. NCT00467025 was removed from this ovarian program because it is a phase 2 renal-cell-carcinoma study. Trebananib directly engages both ANGPT1 and ANGPT2; neither is designated the unique primary protein target. Broader program disposition remains under review.

The adenosine A1 receptor antagonist was evaluated in the paired PROTECT-1 and PROTECT-2 phase 3 protocols. The combined primary publication found no significant benefit on the prespecified three-category clinical outcome versus placebo. Both registry protocols completed; safety findings are not substituted for the primary efficacy result.

The monovalent anti-MET antibody was combined with erlotinib in the completed METLung phase 3 trial after prior platinum chemotherapy. The primary overall-survival endpoint was not improved versus placebo plus erlotinib; median OS was numerically shorter in the onartuzumab arm. The row previously misclassified this antibody as a small molecule.

DLL3-directed antibody-drug conjugate. MERU maintenance therapy was terminated after overall-survival futility in DLL3-high disease; TAHOE second-line therapy completed with inferior overall survival versus topotecan. Trial outcomes are distinct and should not be collapsed into a generic stop reason.
Promoted pilot batch; verify all program-level evidence before publication.

The published BRISK-PS negative overall-survival result belongs to completed NCT00825955. NCT01108705 was a distinct Asia-Pacific phase 3 study marked terminated in the registry without a stated why-stopped reason; it must not inherit the BRISK-PS endpoint result. Bristol Myers Squibb reported termination of the broader brivanib program during 2012 but did not attribute this protocol's stop to a specific endpoint or decision. Brivanib inhibits VEGFR and FGFR proteins without a unique primary protein assignment. The separate renal-cell-carcinoma NCT01253668 protocol is not part of this indication-level program.

NCT01253668 enrolled 10 participants and was terminated after the manufacturer decided not to pursue additional research in this patient population. Its posted outcome data were unavailable after the principal investigator left the institution; no failed efficacy endpoint is established. This is distinct from brivanib's HCC trials.

The randomized phase 3 NCT01009593 trial failed its prespecified overall-survival superiority and noninferiority criteria versus sorafenib. Time to progression and response rate favored linifanib while adverse events were more frequent. The registry says an independent monitoring committee recommended stopping but does not state a more specific stopping rationale. Linifanib inhibits VEGF and PDGF receptor families; no single primary receptor is assigned and the clinical result is not a single-protein target failure.

NCT00360867 was a safety-focused extension for patients coming from other motesanib protocols; it was not a randomized efficacy trial. The registry reports termination by Amgen decision without a specific efficacy or safety cause for this extension. This record must not inherit MONET1's NSCLC outcome. Motesanib inhibits several receptor kinases without one clinically established primary protein.

MONET1/NCT00460317 first enrolled squamous and nonsquamous NSCLC. Treatment and enrollment in the squamous cohort stopped after excess early deaths and fatal bleeding with motesanib. The amended nonsquamous comparison did not significantly improve overall survival versus chemotherapy alone despite favorable PFS and response-rate signals. The registry says Amgen discontinued development because MONET1 missed its primary objective. These regimen- and histology-specific findings are not failures attributable to one VEGFR or other protein.

NCT01799889 included several lymphoma and CLL cohorts. Gilead's registry states the trial ended after its decision to discontinue entospletinib development; this is not a demonstrated efficacy-endpoint failure. Published CLL subcohorts reported responses. Cohort-specific outcomes and later development under other sponsors require separate review.

clinical_programs.indication_name: newly diagnosed NPM1-mutated acute myeloid leukemia
clinical_programs.notes: AGILITY/NCT05020665 tested entospletinib plus intensive chemotherapy. Kronos Bio stopped enrollment before the planned sample was reached because recruiting fit patients with NPM1-mutated AML was difficult and post-COVID constraints persisted. The registry and sponsor do not attribute the stop to a failed efficacy endpoint; this is separate from Gilead's earlier relapsed-hematology phase 2 program.

EGFR-directed antibody-drug conjugate. INTELLANCE-1/NCT02573324 was a completed phase 3 survival trial that stopped treatment early after an interim overall-survival futility finding. UNITE/NCT03419403 was a separate phase 3b ocular-prophylaxis study terminated after that cross-study decision; it did not fail a survival primary endpoint. These are distinct trial outcomes within one indication-level program.

GPNMB-directed antibody-drug conjugate. PrECOG 0504 was registered as phase 1/2 but only the phase 1 dose-finding portion enrolled; the planned phase 2 portion was not undertaken after the company discontinued development for this indication. This is not classified as an efficacy endpoint failure.

Single primary protein target remains unresolved. NCT02730884 terminated at investigator request due to low accrual with three enrolled; this is a recruitment event and not evidence of lack of efficacy.

clinical_programs.indication_name: relapsed or refractory germ cell tumors
clinical_programs.notes: Single primary clinical mechanism is unresolved. NCT01055067 stopped for futility under its prespecified Simon two-stage rule; this is an indication-specific event and does not establish MET target failure.

IL-6 binding mechanism confirmed by approved product information SRC-FDA-siltuximab-label. NCT01266811 was a planned phase 3 study withdrawn before enrollment based on another study; it is not evidence of endpoint failure in this trial. Program remains under review for broader myeloma development.

Two separate phase 2 protocols are distinguished. Completed NCT00513071 found zero qualifying PSA responses among 28 patients. Later NCT01267266 stopped after only eight of 31 treated patients reached randomization following a saracatinib lead-in; its planned randomized efficacy comparison was not adequately tested. Saracatinib inhibits Fyn and other Src-family kinases without one established primary protein assignment; neither trial is a single-protein target-failure demonstration.

Balovaptan selectively antagonizes the V1a receptor (AVPR1A). VANILLA phase 2 in adult men missed its SRS-2 primary endpoint despite a favorable Vineland-II secondary signal. Pediatric aV1ation phase 2 and adult V1aduct phase 3 did not improve their Vineland-II two-domain primary endpoints versus placebo; V1aduct stopped after interim futility. The linked phase 3 record includes an open-label extension but is not an extension-only trial. These are indication- and population-specific outcomes, not proof that AVPR1A is biologically invalid.

clinical_programs.indication_name: coronary heart disease and acute coronary syndrome
clinical_programs.notes: Darapladib selectively inhibits lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 encoded by PLA2G7. Completed STABILITY and SOLID-TIMI 52 phase 3 trials did not improve their respective primary cardiovascular outcomes; the separate Mayo endothelial-function trial was also negative. The target is not the secretory PLA2 family inhibited by varespladib.

clinical_programs.indication_name: previously treated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer
clinical_programs.notes: NCT03228186 reported objective responses in a single-arm phase 2 study; its registry says the trial stopped because the pharmaceutical company discontinued the study drug. The observed response rate is not an efficacy-endpoint failure and the registry does not establish why the company made its broader drug decision. Pevonedistat inhibits the NEDD8-activating enzyme complex; no unique primary protein is assigned here.

NCT03319537 is a separate phase 1/2 mesothelioma study with efficacy and dose-finding cohorts; it must not be attributed to the lung-cancer program. Registry termination reason is sponsor termination of the study agreement; an efficacy-endpoint failure is not established.

The completed U.S. Act-Earli-AD phase 3 trial NCT00105547 found no benefit on either co-primary cognition or activities-of-daily-living outcome. Myriad then discontinued Flurizan development; the separate global phase 3 NCT00322036 and open-label safety extension NCT00380276 were terminated after that portfolio decision and must not be counted as independent failed efficacy trials. Tarenflurbil was developed as an amyloid-beta-42-lowering gamma-secretase modulator but a unique directly engaged primary protein remains unresolved; this is not a PSEN1-specific target failure.

The early NCT00948259 trial primarily evaluated safety and tolerability. The separate ARGO phase 2 NCT01350362 study did not show significant clinical efficacy. Biochemical studies document GSK3B and GSK3A inhibition but do not establish a unique primary protein mediating the clinical effect.

The phase 2/3 REACH CDM trial NCT03692312 completed. Its registered primary CDM1-RS comparison did not reach conventional statistical significance (p=0.0514) while some secondary outcomes favored tideglusib. Biochemical studies document GSK3B and GSK3A inhibition but do not establish a unique clinical primary protein. Do not infer that the entire development program was discontinued from this result alone.

clinical_programs.indication_name: coronary artery disease and acute coronary syndrome
clinical_programs.notes: PLASMA and FRANCIS-ACS reported favorable prespecified biomarker outcomes but did not establish fewer clinical cardiovascular events. Later VISTA-16 stopped for futility and possible harm with higher myocardial infarction risk. Varespladib inhibits several secretory phospholipase A2 isoforms; no unique primary protein is assigned and this is not a PLA2G7 failure. The separate intravenous sickle-cell NCT01522196 protocol is recorded under its own indication-level program.

clinical_programs.indication_name: sickle cell disease with vaso-occlusive crisis
clinical_programs.notes: IMPACTS-2/NCT01522196 studied prevention of acute chest syndrome with intravenous varespladib and enrolled two participants. The registry says the study terminated because of a change in company plans; it does not establish an efficacy-endpoint failure or explicitly attribute this decision to VISTA-16.
GRADUATE I and II; antibody binds aggregated amyloid beta represented by the APP target row; trial status and endpoint result are separate fields.
MISSION AD1 and AD2; Eisai and Biogen discontinued development after an unfavorable benefit-risk review.

clinical_programs.notes: EARLY phase 2b/3 and its phase 2 long-term extension; dosing stopped in May 2018 after liver-enzyme elevations changed the sponsor's benefit-risk assessment. Do not interpret post-termination efficacy analyses as the original stopping rationale.

LUSTER-1 and LUSTER-2 tested exacerbations in severe asthma; ZEAL-1 and ZEAL-2 tested lung function in less severe uncontrolled asthma. All four phase 3 trials completed without meeting their respective efficacy endpoints; Novartis stopped further asthma development.

clinical_programs.indication_name: geographic atrophy due to age-related macular degeneration
clinical_programs.notes: CHROMA and SPECTRI phase 3 trials; intravitreal anti-complement factor D Fab did not reduce geographic atrophy enlargement versus sham in the week-48 primary analysis.

Completed phase 3 osteoarthritis studies included efficacy signals and joint safety concerns. Pfizer and Lilly discontinued global development in October 2021 after an FDA Complete Response Letter and negative EMA CHMP opinion; do not label the representative trials as endpoint failures.

clinical_programs.indication_name: moderately to severely active systemic lupus erythematosus
clinical_programs.notes: EMBODY 1 and EMBODY 2 completed phase 3 trials; neither achieved a statistically significant week-48 BICLA primary endpoint versus placebo. Earlier ALLEVIATE supply interruption is not conflated with these efficacy results.

clinical_programs.indication_name: moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis
clinical_programs.notes: SIRROUND-D and SIRROUND-T completed phase 3 trials with positive efficacy results. A subsequent FDA Complete Response Letter sought additional safety data; Janssen then did not pursue global RA approvals and withdrew its EMA application. This is not an efficacy-endpoint failure.

SYNERGY completed phase 2 with a negative primary endpoint; development continued into AFFINITY. AFFINITY Part 1 then missed its primary and key secondary endpoints; the registry marks the combined Part 1/2 protocol terminated because Part 2 was discontinued. Biogen discontinued opicinumab development in October 2020; registry states the Part 2 stop was not based on safety concerns.

The phase 2 SPARK trial tested anti-alpha-synuclein antibody cinpanemab. Registry status is terminated following negative year-1 primary and secondary outcomes; the primary publication reports no clinical or DaT-SPECT benefit and a lack-of-efficacy stop after interim review. Biogen separately reported program discontinuation in February 2021.

PASSPORT tested anti-N-terminal-tau antibody gosuranemab and did not meet its week-52 PSP Rating Scale primary endpoint. The registry labels the study terminated after that result and states there were no safety concerns. Biogen stopped development for PSP and other primary tauopathies but continued the separate TANGO Alzheimer disease study at that time; do not present this as an all-indication stop.

clinical_programs.indication_name: advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma
clinical_programs.notes: GAMMA-1 evaluated anti-MMP9 andecaliximab added to mFOLFOX6 as first-line therapy. The phase 3 protocol completed; the primary overall-survival endpoint was not improved versus placebo plus mFOLFOX6. A response-rate signal did not translate into an overall-survival benefit.

TANGO is a separate indication-specific program from PASSPORT. Its protocol lists safety as the primary objective; the prespecified week-78 CDR-SB efficacy endpoint was not met and the registry says the study was terminated after lack of efficacy following the placebo-controlled readout. Do not imply the primary safety endpoint failed.

The anti-tau phase 2 PSP study was terminated after prespecified interim futility criteria were met. The primary publication found no week-52 PSP Rating Scale benefit versus placebo. The clinical trial stop is attributed to lack of efficacy rather than a safety finding.

The RAINIER phase 2 trial tested an anti-LOXL2 antibody and was terminated when the second interim analysis met prespecified futility criteria. The primary publication found no improvement in progression-free survival

MINDSET was a completed phase 3 trial of the HTR6 antagonist intepirdine added to donepezil. The primary publication found no benefit on either co-primary ADAS-Cog or ADCS-ADL endpoint over 24 weeks. Registry completion is not itself the endpoint outcome.
